code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 536.gz: one Fortran 77 source file (720 lines, 31193 bytes uncompressed) with a sample program 'to encipher 72-bit passwords across machines with 3 different word sizes'. Build selected by activating the C32, C36 or C60 comment prefixes.
code.archive: sha256 a08e12901d4b135f4f68f886ae5cbc2400c25126d728816a8bae43f71fee3ff8 (netlib.org/toms/536.gz as downloaded 2026-11-27, 8666 bytes; gzip header names the member '536', dated 1995-09-06); uncompressed 536.f sha256 7df7b737a39e075787a8e083faf1f995f13e0088de5efa2f228b3b1d7574ae2c
code.note: gunzip to 536.f in an empty directory. Activate the C32 prefixes (replace the first three characters of each C32 line with blanks) to build the 32-bit variant; the program reads its input cards from the C= lines or the file's own data. The shipped text ends with printed output tables (lines 662-689).

field: numerics and cryptographic arithmetic (modular exponentiation on a prime near 2^72)

claim.location: The printed hexadecimal output table in the shipped 536.f, lines 662-673 (header 'HEXADECIMAL INPUT(X) HEXADECIMAL OUTPUT(FX)', produced by the C32 build's format 1 and format 3). It is the only hexadecimal output in the file. The printed octal block at lines 675-687 is labelled TABLE 2A, and the header at 689 says TABLE 2B with no rows.

reference.file: 536.f lines 662-673 (the shipped printed output; extracted with sed -n 662,673p from the uncompressed 536.f, 12 lines, the header row followed by a blank line and ten data rows)
reference.sha256: sha256 a11a9cf1555d153c6f2608c60592b9fcd1f8a8f349953cd740e30e99037f4fcc (the 12-line extract above, computed 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/536.gz; the ten rows are also quoted in paper_value and checked by exact string comparison)

claim.metric: For each of the ten input rows X (18 hex digits, 72 bits) in the printed table, the program's output FX, written by the C32 build's format 3, equals the printed FX string exactly. Claim: all ten rows agree.
claim.paper_value: Printed reference rows (input -> output): 000000000000000000 -> FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF02; 000000000000000001 -> FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFEB4; 000000000000000002 -> 4539285807BE5487E8; 000000000000000003 -> FA996DE7854F3C34DD; FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFA3 -> FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF02; FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFA4 -> FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFEB4; FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFA5 -> 4539285807BE5487E8; 00000000000000005C -> A0190DBCA6F9748AAC; FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF -> A0190DBCA6F9748AAC; 555555555555555555 -> 5AA6C31129CD247368. The paper was not read, so these are the shipped print, not a value checked against the paper text.

tolerance.basis: Deterministic integer output printed in hex; the comparison is exact string equality of all 18 hex digits per row. No numerical tolerance applies. Fixed before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.data_size: None: the inputs are the ten C= input cards in the file header.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The enciphering function is a modular exponentiation over a 72-bit prime, not a closed form, so the shipped printed outputs can only be reproduced by running the algorithm; the claim checks the 32-bit build that the file's own format statements tie to the hexadecimal block.
